subject: Renewal: add west-region isolation zone & standby clusters
messages:
From: Elena Marino <elena.marino@quantumhealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <s.patel@quantumhealth.com>
Date: 2027-03-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal window — request to add west region isolation zone + 2 standby clusters

Jordan,

Our renewal for Redwood Dedicated is coming up on 2027-06-15 and we need to incorporate a functional expansion into the renewal amendment rather than a separate PO. Specific ask: add a new VPC environment in us-west-2 (zone boundary for our analytics tenants) plus two standby clusters to act as isolated failover for the analytics cluster.

Key constraints:
- Data residency: logs and audit events must remain in us-west-2.
- Disaster recovery: ability to flip traffic within 10 minutes for a single-cluster failure.
- Compliance: SOC2 evidence to be included in amendment.

Can you send high-level options (lead time, delta cost, and whether we should extend term to get committed pricing)? We attached our latest usage report for context.

Thanks,
Elena Marino
Director, Cloud Platform
Quantum Health

Attachments: usage_report_Mar2027.csv

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-03-29T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal window — request to add west region isolation zone + 2 standby clusters

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear ask and the usage report. We can absolutely fold the environment addition into your renewal amendment (keeps procurement simpler). High-level next steps:

1) internal sizing + lead time (we typically need 6–10 weeks for a new VPC environment and 8–12 weeks for additional standby clusters if we need hardware provisioning).
2) commercial options: a 12-month term extension with reserved capacity typically gets ~12–18% off incremental cluster costs; 24-month gives ~22%.
3) ops considerations: prefix/KV cache seeding for cutover, network peering, and a canary cutover window.

Can you confirm the expected sustained QPS (p95 tokens per minute) and any additional retention or log export requirements? I’ve looped in Kimberly for pricing and Neha / Karthik for compliance and infra.

I attached a short note with the questions we need answered to firm up a quote. Happy to hop on a 30m call this week.

—Jordan
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

Attachments: initial_config_note.md

Quick notes from my side:

- They want failover within 10 minutes — likely requires pre-warmed standby clusters with KV cache seeding + dynamic routing policy.

Can you draft: (a) pricing spreadsheet with Option A (12-month extension + 2 standby clusters), Option B (24-month extension + discounted reserved capacity + priority provisioning), and (b) an SOW sketch with the cutover milestones and acceptance criteria.

Jordan

Jordan — draft quote below (high level). I attached a spreadsheet with line items.

Option A — 12-month term extension + 2 standby clusters
- New VPC environment (us-west-2): one-time onboarding fee $18,000 (networking, peering, KMS integration)
- Standby clusters: 2 x r-inference.c48 (pre-warmed): incremental $24,000/month
- SOC2 packaging & evidence for amendment: $3,500 one-time prep
- Lead time: 8–10 weeks for clusters; 6 weeks for VPC if no special networking constraints
- Discount: 15% off incremental cluster spend with 12-month commit

Option B — 24-month reserved commit + priority provisioning
- One-time onboarding fee: $12,000 (reduced due to scheduling window)
- Standby clusters: 2 x r-inference.c48 (pre-warmed): $22,000/month
- SOC2 evidence prep: included in Professional Services credit
- Lead time: 6–8 weeks for clusters; 4–6 weeks for VPC
- Discount: 22% off incremental cluster spend with 24-month commit

Ops notes:
- To meet the 10-minute failover SLA we recommend pre-warmed standby clusters with KV cache seeding. Plan a 2-week canary and a dry-run within staging before production switch.

Attachments: capacity_quote_QH_v1.xlsx

Kimberly Park
